Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the West Indies' second innings! The Sri Lankan players are walking out to the middle and they are followed by Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell. Suranga Lakmal will start with the ball.

West Indies, on the other hand, would be disappointed. They were in charge of the this game when this innings started but things fell away after they got the wicket of Karunaratne early. Since then, they were just punished by the Sri Lankan batters and they have a huge task in hand. They did remove the last five batters quickly after Tea but it might be too late. They now need 376 runs to win and they should take inspiration from their win over Bangladesh just over a month back where they chased down around 400 so they are not out of it yet but they need to bat very well if they want to chase it down. Join us for the chase in a while.

Sri Lanka lost Dimuth Karunaratne early but Oshada Fernando were superb on Day 3. Both reached their respective 50s and they got Sri Lanka back in the game but they lost three in quick succession before Dhananjaya de Silva and Pathum Nissanka got them to safer shores. On Day 4, de Silva fell early but Nissanka and Dickwella played beautifully well and took the game away from the hosts with a humongous stand. Nissanka got to his maiden Test ton but Dickwella heartbreakingly missed out on his ton but he should be proud of his effort.

End of a brilliant batting performance from Sri Lanka! They were behind the 8-ball when this innings started but they have played magnificently and have the game by the scruffs of the neck and are on the verge of taking a 1-0 lead in the series. West Indies, on the other hand, would be disappointed with the effort and they have a lot of work to do now.

Sri Lanka have almost batted West Indies out of the game. But discount West Indies at your own risk as they tend to come stronger when their backs are against the wall.  It will be interesting to see how the visitors approach this final session and if they look for the win and look to put the hosts into bat later today or will they look to bat the whole day? It has been tiring for the Caribbean bowlers but they need to be positive. The shoulders are dropping in the field as Dickwella was given two lifelines, first when Bonner dropped him and the next time when a knock was not detected as none of the fielders were interested and the hosts also have run out of reviews. On a hot day, it has been an abject performance from West Indies, both with the ball in hand and in the field.

Nissanka has been flawless, while Dickwella has had some luck but take nothing away from the pair! It has been a phenomenal effort! Another toiling and tiring session for West Indies. There was hope and excitement at the start but that was just false hope. The new ball managed to excite the hosts initially as Alzarri got the better of Dhananjaya de Silva but after that there was hardly anything. The hosts need to find some inspiration post the Lunch break if they are to have a chance of winning this Test. The second session will begin at 1240 local (1640 GMT). Do join us then.

It wasn't an ideal start for the tourists though. They lost overnight batsman and well-set batter, Dhananjaya de Silva early after getting to his fifty. It looked like the new ball would bring the downfall of the tourists, but not to be. Nissanka and Dickwella have played a superb hand. While the debutant has shown patience and determination, Dickwella has played a great counterattacking knock. The duo have stitched a century stand and taken the lead to 257.

Hello and welcome to day 4 of the 1st Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka. The visitors were on the back foot but they showed great fight with the bat and are in a solid position. Not commanding but solid. West Indies, on the other hand, were made to toil hard on Day 3. With the new ball available and the bowlers fresh in the morning, Kraigg Brathwaite will hope the bowlers can have a much better day and restrict the visitors from taking a telling lead. Which way will this Test go? Will this be the last day? A lot of questions will be answered. Stay tuned for further updates.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

This Test in all likelihood is going to last for 5 days unless there is a big collapse from Sri Lanka when they come out to bat on Day 4. The morning session on the second last day of this Test will decide whether the game is going to go into Day 5 or not. West Indies would just want to bowl and get wickets early on day 4 to take control of this Test. They would be aware that batting 4th on this wicket is not going to be easy and so they would look to keep the Lankan lead in check. While Sri Lanka would hope to fatten up the lead as much as they can and then would look to go out all guns blazing with the ball to push for a win. How will the game on day 4 pan out? To find out, join us on 24th March 2021 at 1000 local (1400 GMT). Till then take care, cheers and goodbye!

West Indies bowlers were brilliant in the morning session as they bowled with a lot of fire to send the Lankan skipper back cheaply. But then they were unaware of the staunch Sri Lankan fightback as Fernando and Thirimanne frustrated them to the fullest and the witness was the second session which was a wicketless one. But things changed for them quickly in the final session with the introduction of Kyle Mayers who took his maiden Test wicket and a few overs later bagged another one. Roach after picking the Sri Lankan skipper early in the day too came back to send the set Lahiru Thirimanne back to the hut. After that, the West Indian bowlers came back to their fiery best as they kept bowling tight lines and lengths to frustrate the Lankan batsmen devoiding them of runs but they could not keep that up as Nissanka and de Silva saw the day off. Holder and Cornwall too bowled their heart out but without any success as Gabriel was once again not at his destructive best. Overall a day where West Indies toiled hard for wickets.

After bundling West Indies out early in the day, Sri Lanka would have hoped for a strong start from their openers but the wicket of their skipper put them slightly on the back foot. But Oshada Fernando and Lahiru Thirimanne combined to stitch a 162-run stand which not only wiped off the deficit but also took Sri Lanka into the lead. During the course of it, both went past their fifties. But their departure in quick time hurt Sri Lanka as they lost Chandimal cheaply too. But Nissanka and de Silva ensured that Sri Lanka cross the 150-run mark of the lead as well as they end the day without any further damage.

What is known as the moving day in a Test match turned out to be a sedate one as Sri Lanka batted beautifully and with responsibility this time in their second innings while the West Indies' bowlers struggled to take wickets regularly. Though they managed to pick up 3 wickets in the final session but the day went in Sri Lanka's favour as they managed to wipe out the deficit of over 100 runs first and then take a lead of more than 150 runs at the close of play.

The hosts, on the other hand, would be disappointed.
